scope: Small real-filesystem recovery error paths only; no database, product model, benchmark or stable API acceptance.

input.setup: Create and seal the eighteen original events through actual stable SegmentedJournal; adopt with exclusive source ownership; create an actual archive checkpoint. Every case uses a new directory.
input.preparedIntent: A separate real child invokes prune and exits73 at the actual after-manifest boundary. The callback is only a crash trigger: before exit independently bind actual prepared intent/owner/manifest generation and plan; a stage name alone proves nothing. Do not construct/edit intent or source metadata.
input.recovery: A new ManagedSource recovers the exact real prepared plan with explicit exclusive_recovery=True; no retry or cleanup after failure observation.

newProtocolBoundary.description: The last potentially failing store-directory synchronization is executed while the original owner-bound operation.lock path exists and its OS mutex is still held. Only after successful synchronization may the temporary mutex be unlocked/closed/unlinked; no subsequent synchronization is required for that temporary mutex deletion.
newProtocolBoundary.notAssumed: Do not assume operation.lock deletion itself is durable, nor that its absence alone means source completeness. A stale reappearing mutex may conservatively reject later work.

faultQualification.actualCall: Patch only the actual directory-sync primitive at its terminal protected-release callsite; call all earlier syncs normally. Freeze the specific bound source callsite after r4 code is available.
filesystemEvidence: Resolved actual sync target equals this case store.
Actual operation.lock is a regular file whose contents match the prepared nonce/token; bind its bytes, device/inode or equivalent file identity.
Independently attempted native nonblocking OS lock on a separately opened handle/child is denied because the owner mutex is held; unexpected OS errors are not evidence of ownership.
Actual manifest is finalized with pending=null/completedPlan matching the prepared plan; actual prune intent has been removed.
Bind archive/index/cache/source-fence bytes and the actual call stack/source line. No author boolean/stage callback is accepted as placement proof.
faultQualification.fault: Raise the preregistered OSError exactly once at this qualified actual final sync. If no such call is observed, record not-executed or failed placement; never claim the case passed.

faults: Qualified final directory sync raises OSError; later diagnostic persistence uses actual normal IO.
The same qualified final directory sync raises OSError.

At the resulting actual diagnostic marker persistence request for operation-failed.json, raise a second OSError before its atomic replacement/write can succeed. Qualify by actual resolved marker path plus the retained owner state and actual source callsite, never by an author flag.

guardDefinition.primary: A retained operation.lock with the exact original archive-operation/1 nonce/token, still recognized by a fresh verifier.
guardDefinition.alternativeForFirstCaseOnly: An independently bound operation-failed.json with exact archive-operation-failed/1 nonce/operationToken recognized by fresh verification. Merely returning a guard=true field is insufficient.
guardDefinition.secondCase: Because diagnostic persistence was made to fail, the original owner-bound operation.lock must remain. An absent or foreign marker/lock is a failure.

checks: Prepared child actually exits73 and original prepared bytes are retained.
Fresh verification of the prepared state is incomplete.
Actual final sync placement satisfies both filesystem and OS ownership evidence.
The exact registered IO fault occurs and the operation does not succeed.
Same-instance subsequent verify/operation is refused after poisoning; inspect actual state and public behavior separately.
Fresh instance remains incomplete with an owner-bound durable guard.
All diagnostic marker IO may fail without removing the prior guard.
Original index/cache/source fence/archive and candidate source bytes are unchanged.
resultPolicy: Every original input, child output, injected exception, actual FS snapshot, owner proof and candidate hash is retained. No failure is inverted, deleted, treated as expected success or repaired by a retry. A process crash/resource/unsupported placement is not a passing safety case.
oldProtocolApplicability: The r3 lock-absent final-sync premise is deliberately not exercised as a success condition under r4. Its old actual3-of9 failures remain unchanged. If r4 has no sync after unlock/unlink, that old target is inapplicable/not-executed, not passed. A new reachable protected-sync error must be tested instead.
